On this page

Your First Run ​

A Run is the durable unit of delegated work. This page takes one from brief to verified result.

1. Start it ​

Two ways in:

  • From chat — describe the objective to PRIME. If it is more than a one-shot question, PRIME calls start_run and you get a Run with its own thread.
  • From the Runs view — the New Run dialog lets you set the brief, the target project, the effort mode, and the execution mode up front.

A good brief names the objective and how you will know it worked:

Add rate limiting to the public webhook endpoint. Done when npm test passes and a new test covers the 429 path.

2. Watch the plan freeze ​

PRIME's first act is to set the checklist. Each ChecklistItem carries:

  • text — the task
  • assignee — the project or agent responsible
  • dependsOn — other task ids that must finish first
  • mode — ask (read-only investigation) or work (writes)
  • acceptanceCriteria — what the verifier will rule on
  • checks / proofs — optional mechanical proof

The plan is stamped into originalChecklist, so any later amendment is visible as drift rather than silently overwriting history.

Guided vs autonomous

Guided (executionMode: 'guided') — the engine picks ready tasks from the frozen plan, batches independent ones, and only advances on a passed verdict. Use it for repeatable work. Autonomous — PRIME decides each step, and can re-plan mid-flight. Use it for genuinely exploratory work.

3. Follow the thread ​

The Run thread is an ordered list of RunEvents. Each has an actor (OPERATOR, PRIME, a project/agent name, or SYSTEM) and a kind:

kindMeaning
messageA normal message
delegationPRIME handed work to an agent
questionAn agent asked something back
answerThe resolved answer
tool / resultA tool step and its output
systemA branch cut, a pause, a cap reached

Every committed message carries its own stats — input/output tokens, cache reads, duration, context occupancy, cost, and the model that served it.

4. Answer when it asks ​

A Run at awaiting_input is blocked on you. Two shapes:

  • A question. Reply in the run thread; PRIME relays it to the agent that asked.
  • An approval gate. If the target project's policy is approval: confirm, a write parks as a PendingApproval naming the exact project, the exact change, and the question. Approving re-runs that precise delegation with approved: true — it is not a guess at what "yes" meant.

5. Read the result ​

When PRIME reports the objective met, the Run goes done. What you have:

  • A branch. Default policy cuts a saidi/* branch and opens a PR; branch: current commits on the checked-out branch instead.
  • Evidence. The engine collects it off git — base ref, commits, files with additions/deletions — plus any command it ran with its exit code.
  • A usage ledger. One entry per settled LLM call: actor, models, tokens, cost, duration.
  • A verification log. Append-only, run-level, and it outlives plan amendments.

Statuses ​

StatusMeaning
activePRIME or a delegated agent is working
awaiting_inputBlocked on your reply
pausedStopped but resumable
donePRIME reported the objective met
errorA turn failed
cancelledYou stopped it

You know the Run worked when…

The plan shows every task at done, the verification log has an entry per criterion with a check the Run did not author, and git log on the saidi/* branch shows the commits. Anything less is a report, not a result.
